pr_body:
tests: lib: cmsis:transform: cf64 min_ram 128k

tests/lib/cmsis_dsp/transform/ with config:
   * libraries.cmsis_dsp.transform.cf64
Needs more than 64k RAM.
128k is sufficient if tests steps are reordered
(decreasing malloc size)

Fixes #27849
pr_comments: Not urgent to be merged before the 2.4 freeze - this is probably fixing a bug, so it can be dealt with later.

issue_context.title: tests: lib: cmsis_dsp: transform: malloc out of memory
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
When running tests/lib/cmsis_dsp/transform/ on nucleo_f207zg,
with config: libraries.cmsis_dsp.transform.cf64 ,
`malloc()` failed as it runs out of memory.
Please note that nucleo_f207zg has 128k RAM (whereas there is a min_ram of 64)

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. sanitycheck -N --device-testing --hardware-map ../map.yaml -c -T tests/lib/cmsis_dsp/transform/ -p nucleo_f207zg
2. See error

**Expected behavior**
Test passed

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Linux and Windows)
 - Toolchain Zephyr SDK
 - Commit SHA: 70ff1d73c42f2e174c49b1e217712b52ad6ae78b


**Analysis**
`malloc()` fails as it runs out of memory when it reaches step: `test_arm_cfft_f64_cmplx_noisy_4096`

    `DEFINE_TEST_VARIANT4(arm_cifft_f64_cmplx, step_4096, &arm_cfft_sR_f64_len4096,`
        `	in_cifft_step_4096, in_cfft_step_4096,  `**8192**);


Analysing further I faced 2 issues:

1) testcase.yaml has a min ram property for this config
`    min_ram: 64`
But while executing step `test_arm_cfft_f64_cmplx_noisy_4096` there is a malloc() of length:
8192 * sizeof(float64_t) = 8192 * 8 = 64k
but we need more RAM for variables, stack, ...
so 64K RAM is no enough.

2) I don't know exactly how malloc() algorithm from newlibc is working,
but it appears during my debug session that even if memory is freed between each step,
each time the size of the malloc is increased, the previous memory size is 'lost' (probably due to heap fragmentation).
So with current implementation before reaching step 4096, we loose 256 + 512 + 1024 + 2048 + ... + 16k + 32k, which is almost 64k lost. And  then it is no more possible to request 64k besides. Finally my 128k RAM are not enough.
If I reverse the order of the test steps : starting from 4096 and decreasing to 16, then test is passed.
Probably malloc() algorithm is able to reuse big memory chunk for smaller malloc which reduce fragmentation.

So 128k is  sufficient to run the test, but it needs changes.

Note: there is no problem with config libraries.cmsis_dsp.transform.rf64 because the max malloc is for `test_arm_rifft_f64_real_noisy_4096`
4096 * sizeof(float64_t) = 4096 * 8 = 32k
comments: Left some comments in the PR #27850.

review_comments:
From #27849, re:
> I don't know exactly how malloc() algorithm from newlibc is working,
> but it appears during my debug session that even if memory is freed between each step,
> each time the size of the malloc is increased, the previous memory size is 'lost' (probably due to heap fragmentation).

IMO, this needs more investigation. I am not sure if fragmentation is the cause as far as this test goes (there aren't all that many mixed-size mallocs here to begin with -- all the allocated blocks are freed before subsequent different-size mallocs); rather, it seems there is something strange going on.

IMO fragmentation is the issue:
When test was in increasing order, the return of malloc() was respectively:
0x200017A8
0x200018B0
0x20001AB8
0x20001EC0
0x200026C8
0x200036D0 (step 512, malloc 0x2000)
0x200056D8 (step 1024, malloc 0x4000)
0x200096E0  (step 2048, malloc 0x8000)
Each time the malloc pointer is a bit more than the previous malloc.
I can just assume malloc algo can reuse freed chunck for smaller malloc but cannot reuse for lager one.
